new_techniques.what: A Consistency LoRA for FLUX.2 Klein 9B (image-edit mode) that locks unmodified structure/identity across repeated iterative edits, preventing the compounding drift where a face edit slowly warps the background or clothing over several passes.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: Multi-step edit chains (face, then outfit, then background) are a common production pattern and this directly targets the failure mode of drift across iterations that the skill's ReferenceLatent/editing coverage doesn't currently address.
new_techniques.where_it_belongs: references/characters.md (multi-reference/editing section) or references/setup-and-workflows.md (image-edit template §), alongside the existing ReferenceLatent coverage

new_techniques.what: A community ComfyUI node pack (ComfyUI-Flux2-INT8) and reports of INT8 quantization giving roughly 1.5-2x faster inference on GPUs like the RTX 3090 for FLUX.2, distinct from the FP8/NVFP4/GGUF paths the skill already documents.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: If corroborated, INT8 would be a fourth quantization option worth a VRAM/speed row alongside fp8mixed, NVFP4, and GGUF — but this is currently a single, unverified community report.

new_techniques.what: diffusers 0.40.0 ships Flux2KleinKVPipeline: on the first denoising step it runs reference-image tokens through the forward pass and caches their attention K/V projections, then reuses the cache on later steps instead of recomputing — a diffusers-native counterpart to the ComfyUI 9B-KV template already in the skill.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: Gives Python/diffusers users the same fast repeated-reference-editing path that was previously ComfyUI-only in this skill's coverage.
new_techniques.where_it_belongs: SKILL.md diffusers paragraph + references/setup-and-workflows.md diffusers section, next to the existing Flux2Pipeline/Flux2KleinPipeline coverage
